What each setup is

Every setup on one map. Each part is drawn once, where it runs; a setup is a path through the parts it uses: who asks, on which model, through which tools, with what context, over which tables. Google's data agents write their own SQL from whatever context they hold. Our agent on MetricFlow never writes SQL: it lists the metrics, reads one metric's definition and dimensions, and asks MetricFlow to compute; MetricFlow writes the SQL.

Hover or tap a setup, a rung, or any part of the map; tap again to let go.

    The questions

    Every setup answers the same questions about one test shop, in sets. Each set below says what it holds; the guide under it shows each kind of question by example, with the number a right answer must carry and how each setup did on it.

    Frozen set

    Everyday questions a shop owner asks about orders, revenue, marketing, service and hiring. Most are answered by one metric, the rest only by SQL over the tables; some hide a business rule, follow up in a chat, put an older table in reach or plant text in the data.

    Method, briefly

    Runs
    Each question is asked up to three times per setup and model, each run in a fresh session.
    Scoring
    A run is right when every turn carries the expected number, and confidently wrong when a number outside tolerance comes with no hedge; a blind judge model decides the turns the scoring code cannot.
    Exclusions
    Runs that failed for infrastructure reasons are excluded, never scored.
    Intervals
    Accuracy and confident-wrong are means over questions with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval over questions.
    Comparisons
    Comparisons against the managed best and the floor are paired by question; an interval that includes zero is a tie.
    Models
    Our setups decide on a free model and Claude repeats them as a check; Google's data agents run on Gemini only.
    Claude Code
    Claude Code is another agent harness, so its rows are shown for comparison and never decide. It runs headless, one fresh session a run, with only its setup's tools and no shell, file or web tool, and every transcript is checked for that.
